rationale: Both are compact and correct and share the same isVowel helper. A is clearer about the rules. It has doc comments, a descriptive helper name (translate rather than word), and a single loop whose break conditions are each labelled with the rule they implement (vowel, the qu digraph, y after consonants). Its empty-word guard means it cannot panic on an empty string. B is shorter and clever: it starts at index 1 so that 'y' is excluded automatically, then patches up qu afterwards. That logic is less obvious, because the reader has to reason about why starting at 1 handles Rule 4 and why the qu check after the loop covers both leading and embedded qu. B would also panic on an empty word if called directly. A's explicit, self-documenting approach is better for maintainability.
